audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart said Skill/Skill/Skill/Teemo/Skill/Teemo/Teemo, giving Teemo levels 4-5 and 2+ items. The packet's derived chart is Teemo/Teemo/Skill/Skill/Skill/Teemo/Sett.
audit.why: Teemo owns levels 1-2 outright: 680 range, Blinding Dart erases Pit Grit, and Sett has no gap-closer until Facebreaker at 3. Levels 4-5 are NOT Teemo's - Knuckle Down falls 9s to 6s and Facebreaker 16s to 11.5s while Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank, so his step-ups speed up and yours do not. At 2+ items a 49.5% win rate plus tank durability and an 80s Show Stopper favours Sett.
audit.corrected: Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Skill, Skill, Teemo, Sett with ratings 7/7/5/5/5/7/4.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] claimed Liandry's makes poison 'burn through Sett's grit bar passively - he stores less true damage'. That is inverted.
audit.why: Riot's Haymaker text: 'Sett passively stores damage he takes as Grit.' Poison ticks are damage he takes, so Teemo's DoT FILLS the bar rather than draining it. The level-6 spike also mislabelled R as a suppression that beats blind; the real point is that blind only affects basic attacks, so every Sett spell ignores it.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten: L1 = Blinding Dart vs Pit Grit with no gap-closer; L6 = 400-range Show Stopper on a 120s rank-1 cooldown that blind cannot answer; 1st item = Liandry's kills but also feeds Grit; Late = 80s R with grounding, true-damage Haymaker centre.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json W and R descriptions and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: Fabricated ability name 'Blinding Shot' used throughout (real name Blinding Dart). Not one Sett ability was ever named. Facebreaker was described as a 'grab-stun' unconditionally. Sett's R was described as suppressing 'through your blind' as if blind might otherwise apply to it.
audit.why: Facebreaker: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him... If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' In a 1v1 with your wave behind you it is a slow, not a stun - and Sett standing between you and your minions is what converts it. Blinding Dart blinds basic attacks: it eats Pit Grit's alternating punches and both of Knuckle Down's max-health empowered attacks, but Haymaker, Facebreaker and The Show Stopper are spells and are unaffected. Cooldowns: Knuckle Down 9/8/7/6/5, Haymaker 18/16.5/15/13.5/12, Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 at 490 range, The Show Stopper 120/100/80 at 400 range. Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at all ranks at 680 range; only its duration scales.
audit.corrected: All real names used; blind-affects-basic-attacks-only stated; the Facebreaker both-sides stun condition stated with the wave-positioning counterplay; Haymaker's true-damage centre called out as unreduced by armour or MR; R's 400 range and 120s rank-1 cooldown given as the actual safe window.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns listed generic placeholders ('Your committal tool', 'Your ultimate') with no numbers.
audit.why: Real numbers make the advice actionable: Haymaker 18s at rank 1, Facebreaker 16s, The Show Stopper 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the three punishable cooldowns and their conditions.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[2] 'Get E-stunned' carried a description about shrooming lane-center bushes - the text did not match its heading.
audit.why: The don't and its explanation were unrelated, and the stun is conditional in the first place.
audit.corrected: Description now states the both-sides stun condition and the wave-positioning fix.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing recorded about the scope of blind, Pit Grit's missing-health regeneration, or The Show Stopper's grounding.
audit.why: Pit Grit gives health regeneration scaling with missing health - that is the sustain anti-heal answers, and it was never mentioned. The Show Stopper carries a grounding flag on its landing zone.
audit.corrected: Added to the late-game text, the first-item spike (anti-heal timing) and the late spike (grounding cuts dashes).
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json P description and R flags

edits.before: At level 1 Sett wants to walk up and throw his passive double-punch, but Blinding Shot turns the second auto into a whiff and immediately reverses the trade. Auto him once with Toxic Shot poison active, fire Q into his face, and back off with Move Quick before he can respond. He has no gap-close at this stage so every time he steps forward you repeat the pattern. The danger is greed: if you keep autoing after the blind instead of retreating with W he will eventually absorb enough poison into his W grit bar for a damaging smash, so one Q and out is the correct loop.
edits.after: At level 1 Sett walks up to throw Pit Grit — his autos alternate left and right, the right punch stronger — and Blinding Dart makes the sequence whiff. Auto him with Toxic Shot active, dart him, step off with Move Quick. He owns no gap-closer until Facebreaker at 3, so repeat it every time he steps up. The danger is greed, and not for the reason you think: Haymaker banks the damage he TAKES as Grit, so your poison fills his bar rather than draining it. One dart and out. And never let him stand between you and your own minions — Facebreaker stuns only when it pulls from both sides; from one side it is a slow.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your lane-control peak. Q is max-ranked so the blind duration is long enough that even if Sett walks through it he cannot profitably auto during the window, and your shrooms are now covering the tribush and the two jungle entrances flanking the lane. He has to walk around or through them to reach you, which slows every approach and keeps you in poke range. At level 6 the dynamic shifts: his R suppresses you through Blinding Shot — you cannot blind him during the cast — and a full W grit dump post-suppress is a genuine one-shot threat. Start mushroom-warding the escape routes behind you before he hits 6 so you always have a safe path out, and never stand still near him because he will bait your passive camouflage and then R you while you are invisible and rooted in place thinking you are safe.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a cooldown crunch and it runs against you. Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank — only the blind's duration grows with points — while Knuckle Down drops to 6s and Facebreaker to 11.5s, so his step-ups start arriving faster than your answer comes back. Hold the 680 line, because Facebreaker only reaches 490, and keep your own wave behind you so the pull slows you instead of stunning you. At 6 the math changes hard: The Show Stopper needs only 400 range, and blind stops basic attacks and never spells, so nothing in your kit answers the grab itself. What answers it is the cooldown — 120 seconds at rank 1, the longest downtime he will ever have. Shroom your escape routes before he hits 6, and treat his ultimate as up until you have watched him spend it.

edits.before: Your first item is the strongest window you will have all game: Liandry's DoT ticks eat through Sett's naturally high HP and drain the grit he would use to smash you, and mushroom-warded side lanes mean he cannot chase you down without triggering a slow-and-damage chain. Past two items Sett's raw durability and team-fight R threaten to outpace your poke DPS, especially if your team needs you in fights where his one-suppression engage lands on your carry. Translate your early poke lead into tower plates and a vision-warded split — the longer this game goes in a teamfight meta, the more the lane's EVEN verdict tilts his way.
edits.after: Your first item is the cleanest window in the game: Liandry's plus Toxic Shot outruns the missing-health regeneration Pit Grit hands him, and buying anti-heal early cuts that regen further. Mushroom-warded side lanes mean he cannot cover the 400 units to The Show Stopper without being slowed and revealed first. Past two items his durability wins the argument — Haymaker's centre is true damage, so the magic resist and armour you buy do nothing against it, and an 80-second Show Stopper lands on your carry whether or not you blinded him. Convert the early poke lead into plates and a shroomed split before the teamfight phase hands the EVEN verdict to him.

notes:
PACKET DEFECT: tools/audit-run/packets/teemo.json has games:null for sett - the ONLY null of 71 entries - but champ-data/content/teemo.js line 9 has MC_REAL_GAMES.teemo.sett = 2186, appended out of alphabetical order at the end of the object, so the packet was almost certainly generated before that key existed. Real data exists, so I audited rather than deferring. If the deferral rule is meant to key strictly off the packet field, discard this file.

LEVEL CHART: proposed as one atomic group across BOTH layers (content win[0..6] and full phases[N].side plus phases[N].rating). It matches the packet's derived chart on all seven rows.

NO MIRROR: audits/top/sett__teemo.json does not exist, so nothing was reusable and nothing was contradicted. Whoever audits sett vs teemo must land on Sett/Sett/Skill/Skill/Skill/Sett/Teemo with inverted ratings 3/3/5/5/5/3/6, and must state the same two decisive facts: blind hits only basic attacks, and Facebreaker stuns only when it pulls from both sides.

BIGGEST FACTUAL FIX: the old text told the player their poison DRAINS Sett's Grit. Haymaker stores damage he TAKES, so chip poke was actively charging the ability the page told them to fear.
